cim: Impact of Artificial Intelligence, budget bill and lobbying laws on the agenda
cim_eredeti: Impact of Artificial Intelligence, budget bill and lobbying laws on the agenda
szoveg_eredeti:
What’s on the agenda for the House and Senate committees today.

Two more committees are set to take a closer look at how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is playing out in areas covered by their respective parliamentary mandates, starting with STATUS OF WOMEN, which is poised to embark on a self-initiated review on how AI is affecting on “women, girls and 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals” with Digital Moment CEO Indra Kubicek, as well as representatives of the Canadian Council of Innovators and Women’s Health Collective Canada. (11 a.m.)

Later this afternoon, members of the SUBCOMMITTEE ON INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS will dig into the “global impacts of AI on human rights movements” with representatives of the Institute on Resilience and Urban Innovation, ControlAI and United Nations Special Rapporteur for the Rights to Freedom of Peaceful Assembly and of Association Gina Romero. (3:30 p.m.)

Meanwhile, FINANCE members have blocked off one hour to hear from Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon as they continue to go through the fine print of Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne’s omnibus plan to roll out additional measures included in last year’s budget. (5:15 p.m.)

ACCESS TO INFORMATION, PRIVACY AND ETHICS members resume their statutory review of federal lobbying laws during a briefing session with Lobbying Commissioner Nancy Bélanger. (11 a.m.)

Senior officials with the Canadian Mental Health Association, Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction and the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health, as well as Gattuso Centre for Social Medicine executive director Andrew Boozary and journalist Adam ZIvojinovic will weigh in on the “opioid epidemic and toxic drug crisis in Canada,” which is currently under scrutiny at HEALTH. (11 a.m.)

NATURAL RESOURCES members look at “Canada’s nuclear future” during a roundtable discussion with representatives of the Canadian Nuclear Association and Canadian Nuclear Laboratories. (11 a.m.)

FOREIGN AFFAIRS members host back-to-back panel discussions on the “effectiveness of international institutions” with Canadian Forces College professor Adam Chapnick and other high-level academic experts. (11 a.m.)

PUBLIC SAFETY AND NATIONAL SECURITY members kick off their review of Conservative MP Dane Lloyd’s backbench proposal to designate the refusal to provide information on the location of bodies or remains as an aggravating factor in sentencing with an opening presentation from Lloyd, who will be joined by fellow Conservative MP Michael Cooper, as well as commentary from Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime Benjamin Roebuck, as well as senior departmental officials. (11 a.m.)

PUBLIC ACCOUNTS members revisit the annual public accounts for 2024 and 2025 with C.D. Howe Institute president emeritus William Robson and research officer Nicholas Dahir. (3:30 p.m.)

NATIONAL DEFENCE members continue to explore the “modernization of the Canadian army” with retired lieutenants general Stuart Beare and Michel Maisonneuve. (3:30 p.m.)

Members of the City of Ottawa Veterans Task Force, Helmets to Hardhats and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, as well as Veterans Legal Assistance Foundation chair — and former New Democrat MP — Peter Stoffer provide their respective perspectives on “civilian recognition of military skills” at VETERANS AFFAIRS. (3:30 p.m.)

FISHERIES AND OCEANS members get an update on Atlantic salmon population from Fort Folly First Nation, Spruce City Wildlife Association and the Foundation for Conservation of Atlantic Salmon. (3:30 p.m.)

On the Senate side, Secretary of State for Defence Procurement Stephen Fuhr will provide his perspective on Canada’s current procurement strategy, as well as overall defence spending, during an afternoon appearance at NATIONAL SECURITY, DEFENCE AND VETERANS AFFAIRS, with Defence Investment Agency CEO Doug Guzman also expected to be at the table. (4 p.m.)
